one_month_reasoning: Full Q3 2026 results should land around Nov 9-10, after Oct 31. But TeraWulf issued preliminary Q3 2025 results on Oct 28 2025 alongside a deal announcement, so an in-window preliminary print or deal release is possible, and it could go either way. Other possible in-window items: launch or pricing of the ~$3.5B Morgan Stanley-led Justified loan/high-yield financing (still unpriced as of Oct 1; a clean print helps, wide pricing or a delay hurts), confirmation of the CB-4 first-hall delivery (targeted late Sept; nothing announced yet), the Morgantown closing (FERC approved Jul 29), and the Oct 28 FOMC. There have been no company releases since Aug 24. Momentum is negative: steady insider Form 4 sales, ~50% below the 52-week high, and Q2 a large miss. Short interest of ~29% of float offsets that with squeeze risk. I centre at ~$14.7 (a slight negative tilt) with a monthly lognormal sigma of 0.26 (91%/3.5), close to round 1. Round 4: unchanged. Site coverage and the split discount rate change the 12-month fair value by ~$0.5 and are not in-window events. The one in-window site item is CB-4's commencement (targeted late Sept, still unconfirmed on Oct 2). A confirmation would also trigger the next Google backstop tranche and lift the $75M revolver cap, but it is largely expected, and a slip would be a mild negative. That is symmetric enough to leave the ladder alone.

fair_value.method: 40/30/30 blend: split-rate DCF $5.85 at the horizon (8.7% on Google-backstopped Fluidstack rent, 9.75% Anthropic, 10.25% Core42 and unbacked Fluidstack, 11% for everything uncontracted and post-term; every inventory site valued once), 12x 2028 EBITDA of $1.205B less $8.12B end-2027 net debt ($10.2), and an 8% cap-rate NAV with the pipeline rebuilt site by site ($11.2). 613M diluted shares, debt at face, 6.8% Justified NCI deducted. With a single 11% rate the DCF is $4.78 and the blend $8.3.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Split-rate unlevered DCF Q4'26-2047 plus terminal, every inventory site once. Contracted: Core42 60 MW ($1.1B), Fluidstack 378 MW ($7.2B incl. amendments), Anthropic 401 MW ($19B), 2.5% back-solved escalators, 80% margin, 3% maintenance, 21% tax from 2030. Rates: 8.7% Google-backstopped Fluidstack share / 9.75% Anthropic / 10.25% Core42 and unbacked Fluidstack / 11% post-term, terminal, pipeline. Capex $6.05B. Site PVs today ($B): Core42 0.76, CB-3 0.35, CB-4 1.33, CB-5 1.26, Justified 1.66, mining 0.01, LM-EXP 0.04, Lake Hawkeye 0.02, Muskie -0.01 (development +0.25, acquisition liabilities -0.08, collateral -0.18), Chesapeake -0.01 (development +0.10, purchase price est. -0.17, existing generation +0.07), Abernathy +0.52 = EV incl. pipeline $5.92B; less net debt $2.7B and NCI $0.11B = $3.11B / 613M = $5.08 today, x1.153 (15.3% cost of equity) = $5.85 at the horizon. Single 11% rate: $4.14 today / $4.78 horizon. Bridge from round 3 ($4.0, single rate, horizon): rebuilt at round-3 inputs $4.39 (+0.39: explicit post-term with extension options instead of a 1% Gordon from 2036); + amendments $4.96; + fit-out capex $4.69; + mining and Abernathy PV $4.70; + named pipeline development $5.46; + Muskie liabilities and collateral, Chesapeake price $4.78; split rates $5.85. Sensitivities (horizon, split): GPU life 4/5/6/7 yrs $5.69/5.85/5.97/6.05; all contract rates -45bp (8.25/9.25/9.75) $6.29; Anthropic at 8.7% (IG support finalised) $6.61; contract rates +80bp (9.5/10.5/10.5) $5.28; refresh-default 30% $5.80. Single-rate WACC: 10% $7.91; 10.5% $6.27; 12% $2.22.

inputs_detail.value: 8.7% on the Google-backstopped 44% of in-term Fluidstack rent; 9.75% on in-term Anthropic rent and Justified build capex; 10.25% on in-term Core42 rent and the unbacked 56% of Fluidstack rent; 11.0% WACC on post-term, terminal, mining and pipeline
inputs_detail.derivation: Anchor: WULF Compute $3.2B notes secured on the Fluidstack/Core42 leases, 7.75% coupon / 8.7% effective (10-Q), Ba2/BB/BB, issued before construction, so the 8.7% already prices completion risk. The deck says the $3.2B Google backstop 'fully covers' that debt. Read-across: the Google-backstopped Abernathy notes priced at 7.25%. I do not go to Google's Aa2/AA+ rate: the backstop is a termination-fee/assume-lease option that takes effect only at each lease's commencement (only $600M today). Anthropic is unrated (S&P), IG support is only 'expected', the $4.2B build has not started and the $3.5B debt is unpriced, so it gets roughly the midpoint of 8.7% and 11%. Core42 (unrated, no backstop) and Fluidstack's unbacked residual (unrated, owns no chips) sit close to WACC at 10.25%. LM capex is discounted at the Fluidstack blend (9.6%).

Cost of equity 15.3% = 10y UST 5.29% + beta 2.0 x 5% ERP; pre-tax cost of debt ~8.7% (10-Q effective rate on 7.75% secured notes), ~6.9% after tax (no shield until NOLs are used); ~45% debt at parent market weights ($5.7B face + $3.5B Justified debt to come vs ~$9.1B equity). That gives ~11.0-11.5%; I use 11.0%. Round 1's unsourced cut to 10% is withdrawn; 10% is shown only as a sensitivity.

inputs_detail.value: In-term rents at contract; after each term, 0.88 x escalated rent (extension options continue the escalator) at 11%; terminal at end-2047 with 1% growth
inputs_detail.derivation: Round-3 supervisor: the Fluidstack leases carry two 5-yr tenant extension options at the escalated schedule ($3.7B initial vs ~$8.7B with extensions), so my implicit ~0.85 factor was low. I use 0.88 = 80% exercise at contract rent + 20% non-exercise with ~1 yr vacancy and a re-let at ~70%. The cash flows are explicit through 2047 (end of Justified's term), so Justified's contracted years 2037-47 can be discounted at its contract rate rather than folded into a 2036 terminal.

bear.story: The AI-infrastructure trade de-rates, or stress at Fluidstack or Anthropic makes the market value WULF on contracted cash flow alone at a ~11% discount rate (DCF $4-6). Fluidstack is Anthropic-dependent and Google backstops only $3.2B of the $6.7B Lake Mariner leases. Other routes: the Justified $3.5B financing prices wide or needs equity at a low price; Anthropic's IG credit support, still only 'expected', is weaker than hoped; Justified slips into late 2028; or the New York moratorium spreads to other states. Round 4: the bear price is anchored on the contracted-only split-rate DCF (~$5.1 today / $5.85 at the horizon; $4.8 at a single 11%) and moves up slightly from $5.3 with the Fluidstack amendments. Added routes: Muskie's $0.3B of cash collateral and ~$0.27B more of LOA installments tie up liquidity, and the pipeline is worth ~0 at 11%, so growth needs either cheap capital or dilution.

base.story: CB-4 and CB-5 deliver, the Justified debt closes at high-single-digit cost, and the stock trades around 12-13x exit EBITDA with modest pipeline credit and some further dilution to fund Muskie. The tail of insider selling and the high short interest roughly offset each other. Round 4: +$0.3 from the amendment rent in exit EBITDA.

bull.story: A new 250-500 MW lease (Muskie or Kentucky expansion, helped by the 482 MW PSC-approved power deal) with a hyperscaler or IG-backed tenant, plus strong AI-capex sentiment, re-rates WULF toward 16-18x forward EBITDA and toward the ~$30-33 analyst targets. A short squeeze adds to the move.

thesis_break_reason: Contracted-only value, with debt at face and 613M shares, is ~$5.1 today / $5.85 at the horizon at split contract rates (single 11%: $4.1 / $4.8), and 10x exit EBITDA gives ~$6.3. A sustained trade below ~$7 would mean the market gives the pipeline nothing and is starting to doubt the contracts or the financing: a failed or punitive Justified financing, Fluidstack/Anthropic credit stress, a major CB-4/CB-5/Justified delay or cost overrun, or a dilutive rescue raise. Round 4: kept at $7.0. The split rate lifts the floor ~$1, but the site rebuild also shows the pipeline is worth ~0 after Muskie's collateral and liabilities, so $7 still marks 'contracts only, with doubts'.

reasoning: Round 4 makes two fixes. (1) Site coverage: every row of the checked inventory now appears exactly once. Contracted: Core42 at the filed 60 MW ($1.1B, single-source TCV kept because it fits ~$1.83M/MW), Fluidstack at 378 MW with the July 2026 amendments (+$0.5B to $7.2B), plus the ~$150M parent-funded fit-out in capex; Justified as before. CB-4 is moved to an effective Jan 2027 start (no confirmation yet, and CB-3 slipped). The unbacked Fluidstack share is updated to 56%. Legacy mining is added as a small wind-down stream on power that converts to HPC, so it is never counted with HPC. The generic $1.2B pipeline option is replaced by four probability-weighted site rows, each net of $11M/MW capex and 3% financing fees at 11%: LM-EXP 25% (NY EO 62, NYISO approval), Lake Hawkeye 12% (EO 62 plus Lansing's draft ban, ~3-yr slip), Muskie 40%/30% (signed ESA and collateral posted, first power Q4 2028), Chesapeake 18%/12% (acquisition not closed, Public Citizen challenge). Muskie carries its $50M deferred and probability-weighted contingent consideration and its July cash collateral net of expected return; Chesapeake carries an estimated $200M purchase price (undisclosed; my judgment) and +$80M for the existing 210 MW plant. Abernathy is sale proceeds only; the Fluidstack follow-on option and the international pursuits are valued at zero. At 11% a new lease at today's rent creates only ~$0.9M/MW of NPV, so the 2,082 MW pipeline nets to ~$0. That is the skeptic's main new finding: the growth story needs cheap capital. (2) Split discounting, anchored on the 8.7% effective cost of the Google-backstopped WULF Compute notes; Anthropic at 9.75% (unrated, support 'expected', unbuilt), Core42 and unbacked Fluidstack at 10.25%, everything uncontracted at 11%. DCF: single-rate $4.78, split $5.85 (round 3: $4.0); the bridge is in the DCF inputs. The other methods move with the amendments and the site rows: EV/EBITDA $10.2 (from $9.6), NAV $11.2 (from $12.6, the generic option gone). Blend $8.8 (from $8.3; $8.3 single-rate). GPU-life layer kept (5-yr base; IREN corrected to 5 yrs per its FY26 10-K). Ladder: same method (35% convergence to fair value, sigma 0.75): median $12.15 -> $12.40, P(>= $14.91) 0.39 -> 0.403. Bear $5.3 -> $5.6, base $12.5 -> $12.8. Thesis break $7.0 and the 1-month ladder unchanged. Site table: value_per_share = site PV today (split-rate DCF) / 613M, before corporate items: net debt -$4.40/sh, Justified NCI -$0.18/sh. The rows sum to $9.67, giving $5.08 today ($5.85 at the horizon). Inventory facts checked: I found no factual error. The Q2 2026 release confirms 102 MW energized + 336 MW under construction at Lake Mariner (= 438 MW), and searches confirm the Morgantown price is undisclosed and CB-4 commencement is unannounced. Research this round: the inventory plus a primary re-read of the Q2 2026 release (102 MW energized + 336 MW under construction), 3 searches (Morgantown price: confidential; CB-4: no confirmation; IREN life) and one fetch; no option data. Earlier rounds: Round 3 folds in the GPU useful-life research. WULF is a powered-shell landlord: Fluidstack (which owns no chips) and Anthropic bring the compute, so chip depreciation never hits WULF's P&L. The research matters only where my model depends on tenant GPU economics: (1) tenant credit at refresh time. The research puts economic life well below physical life (H100 rents -50% within ~18 months of the successor, then flat; old chips reprice to the same ~$3/PFLOP-hr as new ones; Nvidia ships yearly; Amazon shortened some lives 6->5). I take a 5-yr base life, the research's own neocloud base, because the strong 2025-26 re-contracting evidence (CoreWeave H100 within 5%, A100 into 2029) comes from a power-constrained market. Lake Mariner's 10-year leases therefore span about two generations, and when the first generation ages out (lease years 6-10) a thinly capitalized intermediary must re-sign its end customer. I model a 20% x 50% expected loss on the unbackstopped ~52% of Fluidstack rent in that window (about -$0.06/share; the Google backstop and Fluidstack's $1.5B September raise keep it small). (2) Re-leasing after the initial terms. Rack density has gone from ~20 kW to 120-140 kW, so a 2026 hall needs upgrades to re-lease to 2036-era hardware. I add a landlord refresh reserve of $1.5M/MW per two generations ($65M/yr at 5 yrs) to the terminal (-$0.24B, about -$0.4/share). The 1% terminal growth already acts as a ~15% renewal haircut, and the research cuts both ways on renewal (scarce energized MW vs falling compute prices), so I leave it. Justified's 20-year direct Anthropic lease is unchanged. Result: DCF $4.6 -> $4.0 at the horizon (5-yr $4.0, 7-yr $4.2, 4-yr $3.9); EV/EBITDA $9.6 and NAV $12.6 unchanged because multiples and cap rates already embed refresh costs; blend $8.5 -> $8.3. Everything else from round 2 stands, including the supervisor's corrections (debt at face $5.725B, $0.53B Abernathy, 613M shares, Fluidstack's $1.5B raise in the credit view). I still keep 11% rather than the supervisor's ~9.5% asset rate, and the GPU research gives one more reason: the tenant is an intermediary with a lease-vs-chip-life mismatch. At 9.5% my DCF would be $7.2. Ladder: with the same 35% convergence weight and sigma 0.75, the median moves from ~$12.2 to ~$12.1, so P(>= $14.91) goes 0.395 -> 0.39 and other strikes fall by <=0.005. The bear price drops $5.5 -> $5.3. The thesis break ($7.0) and the 1-month ladder are unchanged because GPU life is not an in-window event and moves fair value only ~$0.2. Research for this round: the internal notes plus two direct page fetches (TechTimes on Fluidstack, Tom's Hardware on CoreWeave A100s and rack density); no search engines; options data not used. Earlier rounds: Round 2 applies the supervisor's corrections and a few new checks. Corrections: (1) WACC. Round 1 computed ~11% and then used 10% with no source; I now use 11% (10% shown only as a sensitivity). (2) The SOTP no longer deducts G&A twice (the 80% margin is all-in). (3) The ~70% Abernathy NOI margin is dropped: I re-read the Oct 2025 Abernathy release, and it gives $9.5B/25 yrs, $8-10M/MW and a $1.3B Google backstop but no NOI. (4) Flat average rents are replaced with back-solved escalating start rents. This is the biggest change: 2028 exit EBITDA falls from $1.38B to $1.17B. (5) The company's 613M treasury-method shares replace my 609M; debt stays at face $5.725B. (6) The Abernathy sale is treated as closed with $250M received in July, and Morgantown as a separate pending close. New evidence: the 10-Q shows a 6.8% minority interest in the Justified entity (-$0.21B); New York's one-year moratorium on new >=50 MW data-center permits (CNBC, Jul 14) clouds the uncontracted Lake Mariner expansion, so the pipeline option drops to $1.2B; the Kentucky PSC approved the 482 MW Justified power deal (Aug 24); the $3.5B financing is still unpriced; no company releases since Aug 24. Results: DCF $4.6, EV/EBITDA $9.6, NAV $12.6, so the 40/30/30 blend is $8.5 (from $12.3), ~43% below the price. I disagree with the supervisor's ~10-10.5% 'consistent' WACC for my inputs: with beta 2.0, an 8.7% effective debt cost and a limited tax shield before 2030, my numbers give 11-11.5%, so I keep 11%. I also acknowledge that the DCF (11% with 1% terminal growth) is structurally harsher than the 8% cap-rate NAV, which implies ~10.5% unlevered returns with escalators; that is why I blend rather than rely on the DCF alone. For the distribution I do not assume full convergence to fair value in a year: high-vol AI-infrastructure names trade on sentiment and signings, and analyst targets are ~$30. I put ~35% weight on the log gap between fair value and price, which gives a median of ~$12.2 (round 1: $12.8), and use a lognormal sigma of 0.75 (below the 91% realized vol, since part of that is noise). That gives P(>= $14.91) = 0.395 (from 0.42), with fat tails both ways, consistent with scenarios of $5.5 / $12.5 / $26 at 30/45/25%. I found no short-seller report. Research was limited to ~8 follow-up queries; options data was not used.

gpu_life.revenue_decay_path: Unchanged in method: WULF collects contract rent (2.5% assumed escalators) for each term: Core42 to 2035, Fluidstack 10 yrs from 2026-27, Justified 20 yrs. Tenant GPU decay enters as an expected loss of 10% on the unbacked 56% of Fluidstack rent in lease years 6-10. After each term the rent is 0.88 x the escalated schedule (extension options at contract escalators, with some non-exercise and re-letting), less a hall-refresh reserve of $1.5M/MW per two GPU generations ($66M/yr on 438 LM MW from 2037; $60M/yr on Justified in the terminal), with 1% terminal growth after 2047. All post-term cash flows are discounted at the 11% WACC.
gpu_life.note: Horizon values for the split-rate, all-site DCF (today: $4.94 / $5.08 / $5.17 / $5.25 at 4/5/6/7 yrs). Horizon at 4/6 yrs: $5.69 / $5.97. Single 11% rate at 4/5/6/7 yrs: $4.62 / $4.78 / $4.89 / $4.98. WULF and Fluidstack own no GPUs, so life works only through tenant credit at refresh and landlord hall refits. Life still moves value far less than the discount rate: $0.36 across 4-7 yrs vs $1.07 for the rate split and ~$1.6 per 50bp of single-rate WACC. Peer lives corrected per the fact-check: CoreWeave 6, Nebius 5, IREN 5.
